description.p: Stijl is a vector graphics editor for GNOME. Draw shapes, paths and text, arrange them on several artboards and save your work as SVG, PDF, PNG or JPG.
Stijl ist ein Vektorzeichenprogramm für GNOME. Zeichne Formen, Pfade und Text, ordne sie auf mehreren Zeichenflächen an und speichere sie als SVG, PDF, PNG oder JPG.
Stijl es un editor de gráficos vectoriales para GNOME. Dibuje formas, trazados y texto, organícelos en varias mesas de trabajo y guárdelos como SVG, PDF, PNG o JPG.
Stijl est un éditeur de graphiques vectoriels pour GNOME. Dessinez des formes, des tracés et du texte, disposez-les sur plusieurs plans de travail et enregistrez-les en SVG, PDF, PNG ou JPG.

ul.li: Shapes, pen, pencil and curvature tools, node editing and boolean operations
Formen, Zeichenstift, Bleistift und Kurvenwerkzeug, Knotenbearbeitung und boolesche Operationen
Formas, pluma, lápiz y pluma de curvatura, edición de nodos y operaciones booleanas
Formes, plume, crayon et plume de courbure, édition des nœuds et opérations booléennes
Text boxes, text on a path and libraries for colours and styles
Textfelder, Text auf Pfad und Bibliotheken für Farben und Stile
Cuadros de texto, texto en trazado y bibliotecas de colores y estilos
Zones de texte, texte sur un tracé et bibliothèques de couleurs et de styles

Druckfertiger PDF/X-Export mit CMYK-Farben und Beschnittzugabe
Exportación PDF/X lista para imprenta con colores CMYK y sangrado
Export PDF/X prêt pour l’impression avec couleurs CMJN et fond perdu

Ouvre les fichiers SVG, PDF et Illustrator

description.p: Stijl was largely written with the help of AI (Claude by Anthropic); ideas, requirements and testing come from the author.
Stijl wurde größtenteils mit Hilfe von KI (Claude von Anthropic) geschrieben; Ideen, Anforderungen und Tests stammen vom Autor.
Stijl se escribió en gran parte con ayuda de IA (Claude de Anthropic); las ideas, los requisitos y las pruebas son del autor.
Stijl a été en grande partie écrit avec l’aide de l’IA (Claude d’Anthropic) ; les idées, les exigences et les tests viennent de l’auteur.

description.p: Opens OpenDocument texts (.odt) and templates (.ott): the text flows as body text over the pages with its fonts, paragraph formats, lists, page breaks, header and footer; pictures and tables are placed at their paragraphs.
Paragraph formatting: each paragraph can have its own alignment, line spacing and space before and after. Text styles from the library work as paragraph styles.
A more compact Page section with paired margin fields and buttons for page break and formatting marks. Pages can be reordered by dragging only in documents opened from a PDF.
Headers and footers in the notebook, with page number, page count and date fields and an option for a different first page. Grouped objects that push text away as a rectangle share one rectangle.

A Page section in the notebook properties with exact margins, first-line indent, columns, page break and formatting marks. Push text away has its own distance and can follow the outline or a rectangle; the area is shown dotted while the object is selected.

Automatic line spacing: each line is as tall as its largest text, so larger text no longer overlaps; a fixed spacing can still be set and reset to automatic. The notebook always shows the body text settings.
Redesigned ruler handles in the style of the selection handles: small tabs whose point marks the exact position, and pills at the edges of column gaps.
Formatting marks appear only in the notebook. In the presentation, Select Text selects only text, also beneath pictures and shapes.
First-line indent for body text on the ruler. Clicking into the left column of multi-column text now places the cursor there instead of in the right column.

Notebook writing tools: page breaks (Ctrl Enter), formatting marks (Ctrl F10), and column gaps on the ruler that can be moved and resized. Lists and columns now also work where objects push the body text aside, and page breaks are stored as valid XML.

Body text reliably adds new pages when it runs past the last one. Text colour can be set for selected characters. Columns are available for the body text, and in the notebook the text settings fill the sidebar.

The notebook is now for writing: only the text tool, a click anywhere on a page writes, and the properties show just the text settings. Body text lives on its own locked layer. A page ruler like in a word processor shows the margins, which can be dragged; corner marks show the writing area. Rulers are always shown.

Body text in the notebook view: click a page and write like in a word processor. The text flows from page to page, adds pages as needed and removes them again, and makes room for pictures, tables and charts. The text margin is set in the page settings.

Three views per document: Artboards for free illustration, Notebook with pages that scroll one below the other, and Presentation for viewing and presenting with highlighter and laser pointer, optionally in full screen. The view is saved with the document. Editing a PDF now asks first and lists fonts that will be replaced.
Fixes an empty properties sidebar.
Merged table cells are framed as a whole while typing in them. The properties sidebar is always wide enough for every setting, so it no longer grows when a section opens. New presentation icon.

Any table cell can now be split into columns or rows, and formulas follow when rows or columns are inserted or removed. Rotated charts stay in one piece. Explanation texts were removed from the side panel.

A tidier table panel: one menu button for inserting and removing rows and columns, next to merge and split. New tables look the same in every cell. Converting to paths or shapes moved to the right-click menu, and text direction moved to the text settings.

Table cells can be merged and split, turned on their side, and formatted as numbers, percentages, currency, dates or times. Formulas suggest matching functions as you type, and the arrow keys move between cells while typing.

Charts now work out how a table is laid out – names in the first row or column, series in rows or columns – and pick a fitting chart type. Bar and line charts can have axis titles. The header row setting is gone.

Typing into cells of tables in reopened documents works again. Cells can be typed into directly after picking them, moved through with the arrow keys and copied or pasted as text. References can also be picked while writing a formula in the formula bar.

Formulas now cover the common functions of LibreOffice Calc and Excel in four languages, including conditions, lookups, text and dates. While writing a formula, clicking cells inserts colour-coded references. Double-clicking a cell reliably starts typing, and pictures no longer snap into shapes behind a text box.
Holding a picture over a text box, table or chart no longer places it inside; text boxes make room for it instead.
Column letters and row numbers of a selected table now sit in rounded capsules with a soft shadow, matching the selection handles, with a round move grip in the corner.

Picked table cells can be continued with a fill handle (numbers count on, formulas follow) and moved by their border. Pushing text away is now an effect: pictures, tables and charts have it by default, other shapes can get it, and text follows their real outline. Chart legends can be arranged left or right.

Cells of a selected table are picked by dragging, columns and rows are resized at their headers and the table moves with a grip. Rows and columns can be inserted above, below, left or right of the picked cells. Cells and chart labels get all the text settings of the Text tool, and single chart labels can be styled on their own.

Cells, rows and columns of tables and the slices, bars and labels of charts can be picked and given their own fill, stroke and text formatting. Tables and charts can be converted to ordinary shapes, and text boxes now flow around tables, charts and pictures placed in front of them.

New Data tool: draw a table and type into its cells, with spreadsheet formulas, a formula bar and column and row headers while editing. A table can become a chart (pie, donut, bar or line) that follows its data.
Presentation view: full screen, one page at a time, click or arrow keys to go on. The view bar always offers the two other views.
A selected guide shows its settings with the Select tool too.
First steps towards tables and charts: tables with spreadsheet formulas and pie, donut, bar and line charts can be inserted with sample data.

PDF text sits where it belongs: text boxes keep the PDF's line spacing, table cells and list items are no longer merged, and the last line of a box is not cut off. New icons for Pages, Library, Move View and Highlighter.

Viewing a PDF: select and copy text, move the view, and mark text with a highlighter in four colours. Highlights are saved into the PDF as annotations, and annotations already in a PDF (highlights, stamps, filled-in forms) are now shown.
Page and layer rows look alike, and their previews grow with the sidebar.

PDFs open for viewing first: pages in a sidebar, Undo/Redo and an Edit button instead of the tools. Pages can be reordered and removed and saved back as a PDF without changing their content. Edit says which fonts will be replaced before turning the pages into objects.
Pages and artboards have their own sidebar with large previews; drag one to change the order. Undo and Redo moved into the tool bar.
PDF files open as pages in the notebook view: one artboard per page called Page, with the page background. Paragraphs become text boxes, including bold or italic words, split words and accents.
Scale, Repeat, Offset Path and Blend open their settings in the sidebar instead of a window and show a live preview; Apply keeps the result, Cancel goes back.

Shadow, inner shadow, glow and reflection are effects of their own. While editing nodes or guides the properties only show what matters there; Simplify Path moved into the node options. Guides take the colour of their layer.

Align and effects moved to the properties; new objects no longer take over effects. The corner radius of nodes can be typed in, and nodes have rounded handles with a white edge. The floating bar no longer jumps when it opens and closes.
Fixes a build error in 0.9.73.

The floating bar holds actions, the properties hold settings. Align, Combine and Trace open sideways into their options; one Align works for a single object, for objects among each other and for the artboard. Choosing an effect opens its settings in the properties.
New selection handles: rounded triangles in the corners and pills on the sides, easier to grab with a mouse or a finger. They hide while you move, resize or rotate.
Text settings are more compact: size and weight, and line and letter spacing, sit side by side with icons.

Path operations keep real curves: circles stay circles, and new points appear only where shapes cross. The Shape Builder no longer stops finding areas after a step, after moving shapes with the arrow keys, or for some shapes depending on their direction.

Effects turn with an object while it is being rotated. Fill, stroke and text settings for new objects carry over between tabs. A click with the pen at high zoom with the grid on no longer makes an unintended curve. New icons for effects, rotating and flipping.
New icons throughout the interface, drawn in Stijl.
Builds without warnings again.
New: clipping masks, nested groups, offset path, simplify path, repeat (copies with offset, rotation and scale), global colours from the library and printing.

English is now the original language of Stijl, with German, Spanish and French translations. Effects on images (filters, shadow, glow …) and the line ends of dotted outlines are saved again. Damaged or manipulated SVG and PDF files can no longer use up all memory or bring the drawing out of step.

Effects are much faster: they are no longer recalculated when scrolling or zooming a little, frosted glass only updates when something underneath it changes, and the work is spread over all processor cores.
The wood and fur materials were removed.
Frosted glass blurs what lies underneath again; the fill colour lightly tints the glass.

Patterns no longer show thin seams. Shadow, inner shadow, glow and reflection share one “Light & Shadow” section and can be combined. Frosted glass is its own category and works on solid fills. New materials – gloss, metal, brushed metal, wood, fur and velvet – that also change how a 3D effect catches the light.

Every artboard has its own background colour. Export previews show the content again. Inner shadow (direction, distance, blur) and reflection (length, gap) have more settings. Artistic effects keep photos recognisable, and gingham is a true two-colour pattern.
New effects: inner shadow, halftone, risograph and a paper texture. Nine new patterns – gingham, chevron, herringbone, honeycomb, waves, scales, bricks, leopard and terrazzo – shown five per row.

New effects: glow, crayons and oil paint. New patterns: grid, zebra and cow print. Exports show a preview and no longer replace earlier files – a running number or the date is added. Resizing snaps the moving anchor points too.

Tool groups open right in the toolbar – no more right-clicking for ellipse, star or the eraser – and tool settings such as corners or eraser size have their own small bar under the tools. A friendlier start page with evenly sized cards.

Clicks are no longer mistaken for small drags, so objects and points stay where they are. The Curvature Pen shows the line exactly as it will be, including the closed shape over the starting point. Library sections are expandable rows of one card. Layer previews show everything in the file, any artboard can be deleted, and Blend moved to the right-click menu.
Aligning in the properties always uses the page, Align in the floating bar aligns objects to each other. Path operations are now icons in the floating bar instead of a section in the properties.

More compact properties with fewer headings and lines; the Position section is back. Text styles can be saved to the library with a “+” in the text options. The floating bar now offers aligning and path operations for several objects; duplicate, delete and add to library moved to the right-click menu.

Tidier properties: every section is now a GNOME-style card with one setting per row and evenly sized controls. Convert Stroke to Fill keeps the exact look of the stroke, and list bullets and numbers scale with the text.

Follows the GNOME design guidelines more closely: floating tool, view and zoom bars over the canvas, document details under the title, sidebars that float over the canvas in narrow windows, Keyboard Shortcuts and Help in the main menu, Ctrl+Q to quit, better screen reader support and the system accent colour for selections.
Cleaner window: the tools are now in the header bar, layers and library in a sidebar on the left and the properties on the right; both sidebars can be shown or hidden with the buttons at the top.

Layers and Library now open in a panel on the right, so they can be used together with the properties. Artboards snap while moving and can be duplicated with their contents. Text frame padding scales with the text.
Documentation in English; English is now the default language on all systems that are not set to German.
New name: Stijl (formerly Mondrian). Builds for Windows and macOS, update check, robustness fixes for damaged files.
